turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Hi there, I'm just grabbing vitals before the doctor steps in. Can you scoot up on the table?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): I hear you. Blood pressure is one-oh-four over sixty-six, heart rate one-oh-eight, temp ninety-eight point six, oxygen ninety-nine percent, respirations twenty-two.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that alright for seven?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Yeah, those look fine. Doctor shouldn't be long.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. Getting here was a whole thing, they closed two lanes on the interstate and nobody was even working.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): I came in that way too. Sat forever by the mall exit.

[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And it's so muggy my glasses fogged in the parking lot. Her brother's T-ball got rained out this morning, field was a swamp, then the coach tried to move it to four and bailed.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): T-ball's mostly about the snack anyway. My nephew loses a base every week and still wants the juice box.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Exactly. Marcus cried because he didn't get the blue jersey, number three. I said next Saturday, if it isn't pouring.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Mom.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Alright, I'm done, I'm done. He's six, everything's the end of the world.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. Sorry you had to wait. What brings you in?
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): This rash. She woke up with it a couple of days ago, on her belly and both arms, red and bumpy.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Maya, does it itch?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever, vomiting, or trouble breathing?
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No fever, she hasn't thrown up, and her breathing's been fine. She's just been cranky and up a lot.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Got it. Anything new around then, a medicine, a cream, something she ate?

[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's the messy part. Um, she started amoxicillin four days ago, four hundred milligrams twice a day, the pink liquid, for an ear infection. I also started a new cream, hydrocortisone one percent, twice a day, three days ago, 'cause her arms were dry. And Saturday she had shrimp at her uncle's, first time ever.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, she doesn't know if it was the shrimp or the cream or the antibiotic, and honestly neither do I. The rash was there Sunday morning.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): So all three land in the same couple of days. Any allergies?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually, when she was about two she got penicillin for an ear infection and broke out in hives. We stopped it. I've always said she's allergic.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No I didn't.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Honey you were two, you don't remember. Hives, all over. The pediatrician told us to stop the penicillin.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. I'm not going to call that confirmed. You remember hives with penicillin, Maya doesn't, so we'll leave it unsettled. Let me look at the skin.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Red raised bumps over the abdomen and both forearms, plus a few scratch marks. Lips and tongue aren't swollen. Lungs sound clear.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow. It itches. Bad. At night.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There it is. She told me that at three in the morning and then told you no. Worse at night.

[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the itch is real, nights are worse. Thinking out loud, this could be a drug rash from the amoxicillin, or something in the new hydrocortisone cream, or the shrimp. Early on those can look alike, and I can't separate them today.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you don't have a name for it.

[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): No firm diagnosis. I'd stop the amoxicillin and stop the hydrocortisone starting today. Four days is a reasonable pause for a simple ear infection, but call if the ear pain comes back.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired.

[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): I know. For the itching, let's start cetirizine, five milligrams by mouth once a day. Children's syrup is one milligram per milliliter, so that's five milliliters once a day.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Like Zyrtec. What if the rash just stays?
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): If it's still there in two weeks, we can arrange patch testing for the cream and related stuff. Not something I'm ordering today.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And a follow-up visit?
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. I want to see her back in two weeks either way. Emergency room if her lips or tongue swell, if she wheezes, or if the rash takes off fast.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Stop the antibiotic, stop the cream, cetirizine once a day, back in two weeks, ER if she swells or wheezes. Okay.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's it. We'll just watch the ear unless it flares.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Can we go?
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We can. Thanks, doctor.
